subject: Draft SLA redlines - MSA & Order Form
messages:
From: Erik Muller <erik.muller@skylinehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyline Procurement <procurement@skylinehealth.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft SLA redlines - MSA & Order Form

Hannah —

Thanks for sending the MSA and order form. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the draft and pushed a few redlines specifically around SLA targets, credit calculations, and maintenance windows. High level asks from Skyline:

- Uptime target: we proposed 99.95% in the redline but would consider 99.9% if you can accept a global (not per-region) measurement and an explicit calculation method. Please confirm how you measure availability (per-region, per-cluster, or global) and whether the uptime percentage excludes scheduled maintenance.

- Credits: our redline requests an hourly-minute prorated credit (credits calculated per minute of downtime with a 15-minute floor). Your doc uses daily buckets and caps at 50% of monthly fees. We need to align on formula and maximum exposure.

- Maintenance windows: Skyline cannot accept more than one 4-hour weekly maintenance window that may impact production across our US regions. We asked to cap scheduled maintenance to 2 hours per zone or alternatively allow rolling maintenance that does not affect >10% of capacity at once.

- Response & resolution: P1 initial response within 1 hour and continuous updates until mitigation. P2 within 4 hours. Include phone escalation for P1 incidents to a named on-call.

- Timezones: our primary ops are Eastern Time — please call out the baseline timezone for SLA measurement and credit triggers.

I've attached Skyline_MSARedlines_v2.docx with inline comments. Can your team produce a redline back on the same doc with suggested language for: (a) availability calculation, (b) credit formula, (c) maintenance definition (scheduled vs emergency), and (d) an escalation path for P1s?

Appreciate a quick turn on this — Skyline is targeting legal sign-off in the week of Sep 25.

Thanks,
Erik Muller
Head of Procurement — Skyline Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 19 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA redlines - MSA & Order Form

Erik —

Thanks for the detailed redline. We can absolutely work through these items; looping in Jonas (runtime/ops) and Irene (legal ops) to make concrete edits. High-level responses below and we'll push a redline to the doc by end of day Friday (Sep 22) for your team to review: 

- Availability measurement: Redwood measures availability at the deployment level by region by default (i.e., the region's active serving pool). For Hosted customers we offer a global view that aggregates regions; for Dedicated/Private deployments the metric is regional. Proposal: add a clause that availability is measured per-customer deployment and provide both per-region and aggregate metrics in the console. We can add language that clarifies exclusion of scheduled maintenance (with advance notice).

- Credit formula: we prefer a per-incident, per-day credit model with a monthly cap. To find middle ground, propose: credits calculated pro-rata by minute with a 15-minute minimum window for any paid credit, credit tiers matching availability bands (99.99, 99.9–99.989, 99.5–99.899), and a max of 50% of monthly recurring fees unless a higher SLA add-on is purchased. We'll put the exact math into the redline.

- Maintenance: we can accept rolling maintenance constraints. Suggested language: scheduled maintenance will be limited to 2 hours per availability zone (AZ) per week, or alternatively rolling maintenance that keeps >90% of capacity available in any region. Emergency maintenance (security patches) will be communicated within 2 hours and is excluded from uptime calculations if required to mitigate active threats.

- Response times: we can commit to P1 initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes for Dedicated/hosted customers with the SLA add-on; standard hosted tier keeps 1 hour. For clarity in the order form, we'll include a tiered support matrix so Skyline can select the response level that matches the price. Phone escalation will be added for P1s as an option in the order form.

I'm attaching a quick internal note (Redwood_SLA_response_v1.docx) with proposed language and a sample credit table. Jonas — can you confirm if the rolling maintenance wording below is technically feasible across our serving topology? Irene — please flag any legal traps.

Best,
Hannah
VP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
Hannah.Schmitt@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_response_v1.docx (docx)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Erik Muller <erik.muller@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Sep 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA redlines - MSA & Order Form

Hannah / Erik —

Quick technical clarifications from runtime/ops perspective:

- Rolling maintenance: feasible. Our serving runtime supports draining subsets of instances per-AZ to keep >90% capacity; however, for Dedicated and Private deployments where customers reserve GPU pools, rolling maintenance may still cause brief degradation if the customer's pool is small. We'll note that rolling maintenance guarantees apply only when the deployment's capacity exceeds a defined minimum (e.g., >8 GPUs).

- Measurement windows: availability is computed from uptime checks and successful token-serving responses logged by our regional controllers. We can expose the raw event stream for auditing, but per-customer historical granularity depends on retention settings (defaults: 90 days). If Skyline needs longer retention for dispute resolution, that's an add-on.

- Failover behavior: for Hosted customers our multi-region failover reduces customer-visible downtime; for Private/VPC we cannot automatically fail traffic across regions without explicit network configuration. We should add a note that cross-region failover is outside the base SLA unless a multi-region deployment is purchased.

- Support response SLA: 15 minute ack + 1 hour mitigation target for P1 is fine for Dedicated with premium SLA. For standard tiers, 1 hour ack / 4 hour mitigation stays.

I'll mark the technical caveats in the redline so legal has explicit language. Also recommend adding an optional \"High Availability Add-on\" line item in the order form that guarantees cross-region failover and higher credits.

Jonas
Director, Runtime Engineering — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
